driverRegime.method: daily % change of each asset regressed on the daily change in the US 2-year and 10-year yields (basis points) and on the daily % change in WTI; a driver is dominant when |corr| >= 0.4

dataNotes: Run timing: this cycle ran the morning of Thursday 19 November 2026 after the GitHub Actions fetch job drafted contracts/*.2026-11-18.json from Wednesday 18 November's close. Every figure used is dated at or before 2026-11-18; the October FOMC minutes (released 2pm ET 18 November), Anthropic's $83 IPO pricing and Palo Alto Networks' after-hours move are dated 18 November. News-log entries dated 19 November (Anthropic's debut, jobless claims, Philadelphia Fed, gold/silver lows) were NOT used.

Bonds, dollar and IWM sigma are not auto-fetched; the last obtainable implied-volatility values (TLT 30-day IV, EUR/USD 1-month ATM IV, RVX) were carried forward again with stale-source notes. The fetched ^VIX (24.56), ^GVZ (28.04) and ^VXN (33.12) sigma gauges are dated 18 November.

News-log entries for 2026-11-18 (four, matching the Artifact database exactly; already present in data/news_log.json; no hand-entered entries) were read. Session wraps from CappNotes ('Closing Look - Wednesday, November 18, 2026') and Investrade ('Market Review: November 18, 2026' and 'Morning Preview: November 18, 2026') supplied indexes, breadth, sectors, VIX, yields, FX, metals/oil, credit, ETF flows, Kalshi/FedWatch pricing, FOMC minutes, Fed speakers, housing data and movers. AAII figures are from the week ending 11 November (the next release is after S). The 18 November 20-year Treasury auction result could not be obtained.

Vendor conflicts: gold's session change is -3.50% to $3,728.80 (CappNotes) vs -3.16% to $3,741.90 for the December contract (Investrade) vs -2.16% on the fetched GC=F close (3820.4 -> 3737.9; the prior fetched close already reflected part of Tuesday's late decline); the fetched close is used. December-hike odds are Kalshi 91% / 8% larger (CappNotes) vs CME FedWatch ~95% / ~5% (Investrade). The 10-year is -3bp to 5.07% (CappNotes) vs -3.6bp to 5.065% (Investrade); CappNotes has the 2-year unchanged at 4.80%. NQ=F's fetched close was flat (-0.5 point) while the Nasdaq-100 cash index rose 0.42%, and ES=F fell 0.46% vs the S&P 500 cash index's -0.23%, because the prior futures closes were struck at a different time from Tuesday's cash close; the fetched closes are used.

Category 1-12 votes are neutral unless a dated source gives a clear read: Credit (1D) is bearish for the three equity assets on the 20bp two-session high-yield widening; Rates (1D) is bullish for Treasuries on the third straight decline in long yields; Fed path is hawkish horizon-wide (October minutes 'almost all' saw further hikes, Waller's half-point talk, Kalshi 91%) - bearish for equities, Treasuries and gold, bullish for the dollar; Breadth (1D) is bullish for the Russell 2000 on small-cap leadership; Cross-asset (1D) is bullish for the S&P 500 and Russell 2000 (oil, their dominant 21-session driver with negative correlation, fell 3.20%), bullish for Treasuries (oil drop, Middle East strikes, weaker Europe), bearish for gold (silver, copper and crypto liquidated alongside a 19-month dollar high) and bullish for the dollar (broad FX demand); Sentiment (5D/10D) is a contrarian bullish vote for the equity assets on AAII's 51.4% bearish reading. Anthropic's 19 November debut, Thursday's data, options expiry and Thanksgiving week are binary event risk (neutral). Trend structure follows the computed structure reads; Market structure carries its own mechanical direction.

newsLog.event: US stock futures rallied pre-market after Nvidia's Q3 beat and strong Q4 guidance eased AI-trade fears following the S&P 500's four-day losing streak; Asian chip stocks led gains with Korea's Kospi up ~2%.
newsLog.numbers: Nasdaq futures +1%, S&P 500 futures +0.6%, Dow futures +0.2% (~4:45 a.m. ET); NVDA +3% pre-market; ASML ~+3%; Kospi +~2%, Nikkei +0.3%
newsLog.reaction: Tech-led bounce indicated for the open; Fed minutes due today and Palo Alto Networks reports after the bell.

newsLog.event: The dollar rose to a 19-month high as hot inflation data, strong retail sales and hawkish Fed commentary (Gov. Waller urging more aggressive action) cemented bets on a December rate hike; BOJ's Ueda reiterated need for further tightening.
newsLog.numbers: DXY +0.2% to 103.82 (highest since Apr 2025); EUR/USD -0.3% to $1.0965; USD/JPY ~159.41; 25bp December hike fully priced; 10Y Treasury yield slipped back below 5.10%, 30Y ~5.44%
newsLog.reaction: Dollar strength and >5% long yields keep pressure on rate-sensitive assets; FOMC meets Dec. 8-9.

newsLog.event: Gold slid sharply overnight to multi-month lows as the strong dollar and December rate-hike bets weighed on bullion; copper also fell to multi-month lows.
Oil fell overnight as expectations of a supply surplus outweighed concerns about Middle East hostilities.
newsLog.numbers: Brent -1.85% to ~$91.50/bbl (Dow Jones, early trade); Fortune's 6:30 a.m. ET Brent reading $94.21, -$0.73 d/d
newsLog.reaction: Lower crude eases some inflation pressure; energy stocks may lag.
